text:
Alex: Heads-up — we've got a Priority 2 from a customer reporting repeated 429s and "quota_exceeded" errors starting ~10:05 UTC. They say it spikes for ~30s every few minutes and affects multiple routes (chat/completions + embeddings). They included a few sample request IDs but I couldn't map them in logs quickly. Can SRE/Eng help triage?

Maria: @Alex can you paste one of the request-ids and the API key suffix they reported? also, do they see `Retry-After` returned?

Alex: Here are two IDs from the customer: req_01G7X3A2 and req_01G7Y1B9. Key suffix: -abcd. They pasted this response body: `{\"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit\",\"message\":\"quota_exhausted\"}}` — no Retry-After header in their capture.

Dan: Got it. I'll look up logs for the key suffix. Quick checklist: 1) correlate request IDs -> internal request_id, 2) check per-key bucket counters, 3) verify if a model variant fallback triggered, 4) check burst token settings for their account.

Maria: I'm seeing a pattern in metrics — brief bursts in per-key QPS around 10:05, 10:11, 10:16 UTC where the token-bucket refill couldn't keep up. The `throttles_per_minute` series for that org jumps to ~120 at peak. Pasting a dd/Prom query we used: `sum by(api_key) (increase(rate_limit_denied_total{reason="token_bucket"}[1m]))` — you can swap `api_key` to `route` or `model`.

Alex: Nice. Customer says traffic shape changed: a background worker started retrying aggressively after intermittent 5xxs. Sounds like client-side backoff issue causing feedback loop.

Jess: For product visibility, we should ensure support can quickly surface a single dashboard with: per-customer throttles, per-route throttles, 95p latency, model-variant fallback counts, and recent `Retry-After` header averages. We already have panels but they're scattered.

Kevin: Also check billing quotas — if they were near a monthly committed cap we might be enforcing hard quotas. If quota exhausted, responses are 429 with `quota_exceeded`. If it's rate limiting due to burst limits, reason is `token_bucket`.

Dan: To reproduce locally (dev), try this curl that mimics their bursty worker (fast loop, no backoff):

```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-redwood-1","input":"hello"}' &
done
wait
```

You should see 429s after the token bucket drains. Add `sleep 0.2` between calls to avoid it.

Maria: Tools I used to attribute: 1) logs -> `request_id` -> `api_key` mapping, 2) metric series `rate_limit_allowed_total` vs `rate_limit_denied_total`, 3) redis counters for per-key burst tokens (we keep a small dashboard for this). Example redis key pattern: `burst:<org_id>:tokens`.

Alex: Customer wants a quick mitigation they can do on their side while we investigate. Recommended immediate guidance?

Dan: Tell them to implement exponential backoff with jitter (and cap retries) — classic. Also enable client-side rate limiting: p95 throughput smoothing and token-bucket sized to their expected concurrency. Example pseudocode: `backoff = min(max_backoff, base * 2^attempt) + jitter`.

Jess: From product side, we should add an SLA doc blurb about how retry storms can cause enforced throttles and that we return `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and optionally `Retry-After` when applicable. If they don't see headers, ops might have stripped them at the gateway — @Dan can you verify the proxy isn't dropping headers when we return 429?

Dan: I'll check. Initial look: our responses include headers, but some older SDKs/clients might not surface them. I'll verify proxy rules and a couple of SDK versions.

Maria: Alerting suggestions: two types — (A) infra alerts to page SRE when global throttles spike (e.g., `sum(rate(rate_limit_denied_total[5m])) > 500`), and (B) support-facing alerts per-customer: when `rate_limit_denied_total` for an org > 10/min for 3 consecutive 1m windows, create a support ticket but no page. Also surface top offender routes/models in the alert payload.

Alex: What fields should we capture in a support ticket to speed root cause? I'll paste a template to share with customers: 1) sample request-id(s), 2) API key suffix, 3) timestamp window (UTC), 4) route(s) affected, 5) approximate QPS or concurrency change, 6) recent deploys on their side, 7) raw request/response headers (sanitized).

Kevin: If it's quota exhaustion, ask whether they were close to a monthly cap. For dedicated customers we sometimes have different bucket sizes — check account plan. If they need an emergency increase, we might do a transient uplift but that requires billing approval.

Alex: I've asked the customer for the extra fields. Meanwhile, can we create a short consolidated dashboard/tab in Console for support that shows: per-org throttles (last 1h), per-route throttles, token-bucket fill-level, top 10 request paths by deny count, and recent 429 response examples?

Jess: Agree — we should ship a support view. Filing a small PM ticket to prioritize. @Dan @Maria can you sketch the required metrics and panels?

Dan: Will do. Preliminary metric list: `rate_limit_allowed_total`, `rate_limit_denied_total{reason=~".*"}`, `rate_limit_retry_after_seconds`, `request_duration_seconds{quantile="0.95"}`, `model_fallback_count`, `burst_tokens_current`. Panel types: time-series + table (group by org, route, model).

Maria: One quick query I use for attribution in Datadog: `by {api_key}.as_rate(rate_limit.denied{env:prod}.rollup(sum, 60))` then join with `by {api_key}.as_rate(request.count{env:prod}.rollup(sum, 60))` to compute deny ratio. If deny_ratio > 0.02 -> show in support dashboard.

rate-limit-bot: auto-notice — org 0xCDE had 142 denies in last 5m, top route `/v1/chat` (model rw-redwood-1).

Alex: Nice auto-notice. Customer responded with the requested fields and confirms they started a retry loop after ~10:03 UTC with several hundred parallel workers. They also confirmed they don't see `Retry-After` header.

Dan: I've checked the gateway logs. We are emitting `Retry-After` for token_bucket denies but an internal proxy config for that account was stripping custom headers. I pushed a config change to preserve rate-limit headers for that tenant. Will monitor.

Maria: I temporarily bumped their soft burst allowance by +20% for 10 minutes (non-bill impacting) to give them breathing room while they roll a client fix. Note: record in the ticket so it's reversible.

Alex: Customer applied client-side jitter+cap and reduced concurrency by 70% — they report errors dropped to near-zero. I'll confirm again in 15m and then close the support case if stable.

Jess: Action items: [ ] Dan verify proxy header handling (owner: Dan) [ ] Maria record temporary burst bump + monitor (owner: Maria) [ ] Product create support dashboard ticket (owner: Jess) [ ] Support share retry/backoff best-practice snippet with customers (owner: Alex)

Kevin: If they request permanent quota uplift, escalate to billing with usage history attached.

Alex: Closing loop — they sent logs showing no further 429s after client patch. Will leave case open 48h for stability, then close. Thanks all. :tada:

Dan: I'll follow-up with a small PR to ensure headers survive proxy rewrite; will ping this thread when deployed.

Maria: I'll add the per-org deny-rate alert to the support channel once we agree on thresholds.

rate-limit-bot: reminder — follow-up in 24h to check stability for org 0xCDE.
